title: Master Bacon: Skillet Rendering, Water-Assisted Cooking, and Oven Batch Method (Techniquely with Lan Lam)
summary: America’s Test Kitchen’s Techniquely episode with Lan Lam compares classic skillet bacon with a water-assisted approach and an oven-based batch method, aiming for more consistent texture. The video walks through rendering fat in a 12-inch skillet without preheating, then introduces a water technique (quarter-cup for six slices) to control browning and reduce flipping, followed by a full-batch skillet method using water (one cup) and two-layer arrangement. It then demonstrates oven-baking bacon on a sheet pan at 400°F for larger quantities, and ends with explanations of common packaging terms (center-cut, non-nitrite/uncured, thick-cut) and practical serving tips. The transcript provides time-stamped steps, cues for doneness (bubble size and sizzle), and tips on draining and texture, all anchored by concrete timings and measurements from the demonstrations (e.g., 12-inch skillet, one cup water for a full package, 400°F oven).
